Yes, minors (under 18) must be linked to a primary guardian account, and proxy access levels must be configurable.
Query the Master Patient Index (MPI) database using name, date of birth, and gender to match existing records before creating a new profile.
refined_summary: Develop a secure Patient Portal registration system that captures demographics, insurance details, and medical intake information. The system must verify identity via a credit-bureau API and government ID photo upload. It must support digital signatures on HIPAA and Treatment Consent forms with timestamped IP tracking, manage proxy access for minor dependents, and integrate with the clinic's Master Patient Index (MPI) to prevent duplicate records.
functional_requirements: The system shall display separate, secure forms for capturing demographics, insurance details, and medical history questionnaires.
The system shall integrate with the IDology verification API to validate customer inputs against credit bureau files.
The system shall allow patients to sign HIPAA and Treatment Consent forms digitally, storing the output as a read-only PDF.
The system shall allow legal guardians to link dependent patient accounts (under 18) to their primary portal account.
The system shall execute an MPI matching algorithm using Name, DOB, and Gender, routing duplicates to an administrator review queue.
non_functional_requirements: All database tables storing PHI must be encrypted at rest using AES-256 and in transit using TLS 1.3.
The identity verification check must complete in under 5 seconds to prevent registration dropouts.
The application must comply with HIPAA Security Rule, SOC 2 Type II, and HITECH Act standards.
acceptance_criteria: Verify that registration fails and requests manual review if the government ID photo upload is missing or corrupted.
Verify that a registered legal guardian can view the dependent minor's medical profile by switching accounts inside the portal dashboard.
Verify that search queries in the database do not expose unencrypted PHI in system logs during MPI checks.

raw_requirement: Doctors need to show their available slots and patients should be able to book them, reschedule, or cancel.
ambiguities: Rules for scheduling conflicts (double-booking prevention, buffer times between slots) are not defined.
Appointment rescheduling/cancellation window policies (e.g., minimum 24-hour notice, cancellation fees) are unspecified.
The support for different appointment types (telehealth vs. in-person vs. lab work) and their varying durations is missing.
Syncing with doctors' external calendars (Outlook, Google Calendar) is not addressed.
Automated waitlist management when slots open up is omitted.
clarification_questions: What are the allowed appointment types, and what are their default durations (e.g., telehealth vs. in-person)?
What are the business rules for cancellation and rescheduling (e.g., cut-off times, penalties)?
How should the system prevent booking conflicts if a doctor has surgery or is on-call?
Should the schedule sync bi-directionally with external clinician calendars like Outlook or Google Calendar?
Do we need an automated waitlist system that notifies next-in-line patients when a slot is cancelled?
user_clarifications: Support three types: Telehealth (15 min), In-Person Consult (30 min), and Comprehensive Physical (60 min).
Cancellations and rescheduling are allowed up to 24 hours before the appointment. Cancellations within 24 hours are flagged for a $50 fee.
Enforce a mandatory 5-minute buffer between appointments. Do not allow booking during doctor blockouts (surgery, vacation) synced from EHR.
Yes, bi-directional sync with Microsoft Outlook Calendar via Graph API is required for doctor calendars.
Yes, if an appointment is cancelled, automatically SMS-alert waitlisted patients for that day/time. First to respond gets the slot.
refined_summary: Design an Appointment Scheduling system supporting Telehealth (15 min), In-Person (30 min), and Comprehensive Physical (60 min) appointments with 5-minute buffers. Integrate bi-directional Microsoft Outlook calendar synchronization, block bookings during EHR-defined blockouts, enforce a 24-hour cancellation cut-off (flagging late cancellations for a $50 fee), and manage an automated SMS-based waitlist notification system.
functional_requirements: The system shall display available slots dynamically based on appointment type duration and mandatory 5-minute buffer.
The system shall bi-directionally sync appointment blocks with the clinician's Microsoft Outlook Calendar every 5 minutes.
The system shall enforce a 24-hour cancellation rule, blocking self-service cancellation and routing late cancellations to billing.
The system shall automatically queue patients on a waitlist and send Twilio SMS invites if a slot becomes vacant.
The system shall update the appointment status in the EHR in real-time (e.g., Booked, Rescheduled, Cancelled, Checked-In).
non_functional_requirements: The appointment booking API must prevent double-booking under high concurrent load using database locking.
Calendar rendering response time for patient views must be under 800ms.
SMS waitlist notifications must be dispatched within 60 seconds of a cancellation event.
acceptance_criteria: Verify that a patient cannot book a 30-minute slot that overlaps with a doctor's surgery blockout time.
Verify that cancelling an appointment 23 hours prior flags the order for a $50 fee on the billing dashboard.
Verify that if User A cancels their slot, User B (first on the waitlist) receives an SMS alert with a reservation link within 1 minute.

raw_requirement: Build a secure patient chart system that lets doctors read and write clinical notes, allergies, and diagnoses.
ambiguities: Standard clinical data models (e.g., HL7, FHIR, ICD-10, SNOMED) are not specified.
Fine-grained access control roles (e.g., nurses vs. doctors vs. administrative staff) are undefined.
Historical change logging (audit trails) for HIPAA compliance is not detailed.
Handling of sensitive diagnoses (e.g., mental health, HIV status) is missing.
Integrations with external labs and diagnostics networks are omitted.
clarification_questions: What clinical coding standards should be used (e.g., ICD-10 for diagnoses, RxNorm for medications, FHIR JSON formats)?
What roles should have read/write access to different sections of the EHR (e.g., can nurses write diagnoses)?
What are the specific HIPAA audit log requirements for tracking patient record access?
Are there special privacy restrictions or consent requirements needed for accessing sensitive mental health records?
Does the patient chart system need to ingest HL7 v2 payloads from external radiology and pathology labs?
user_clarifications: Use ICD-10-CM for diagnoses, RxNorm for prescriptions, and structure data in HL7 FHIR R4 JSON format.
Doctors have full read/write access. Nurses can write clinical notes, vitals, and allergies, but only read diagnoses and prescriptions. Admins have no clinical access.
Log every single read, write, edit, and export action containing the user ID, timestamp, patient ID, IP address, and specific fields accessed.
Sensitive diagnoses (HIV, substance abuse, mental health) require double-authentication and explicit breakout audit logging ('break the glass' workflow).
Yes, ingest HL7 v2.5 ORU (Observation Result) messages from our lab partner via a secure SFTP/VPN endpoint.
refined_summary: Implement a secure Electronic Health Record (EHR) chart system utilizing FHIR R4 JSON format, ICD-10-CM coding, and RxNorm. Enforce role-based access separating physicians (full access) from nurses (vitals, allergies, notes write-only). The system must log all PHI access in a tamper-proof HIPAA audit trail and implement a secure 'break the glass' authentication workflow for sensitive records, with HL7 v2.5 integration for external lab ingestion.
functional_requirements: The system shall map clinical database models to FHIR R4 resources (Patient, Observation, Condition, MedicationRequest).
The system shall enforce field-level read/write permissions based on the authenticated user's role (Physician vs. Nurse).
The system shall block view of sensitive conditions unless the doctor triggers the 'Break the Glass' override, prompting MFA verification.
The system shall record an immutable log entry in the audit database for every FHIR resource read or write action.
The system shall parse incoming HL7 v2.5 ORU lab files and update the patient's observation records automatically.
non_functional_requirements: Audit logs must be written to an immutable write-once-read-many (WORM) storage system.
EHR page loading and record rendering must complete within 1.0 second to ensure clinic workflow speed.
Clinical note inputs must support autosaving every 10 seconds to prevent data loss.
acceptance_criteria: Verify that a nurse trying to add an ICD-10 diagnosis code receives a 'Permission Denied' alert.
Verify that entering 'Break the Glass' mode on a sensitive chart prompts for a secondary OTP and alerts the compliance officer.
Verify that when a doctor reads a patient profile, a matching read event log is created with the exact fields accessed.

raw_requirement: Doctors and patients should be able to do video calls for remote consultations.
ambiguities: The video streaming technology (WebRTC, Zoom API, Agora) is unspecified.
HIPAA security requirements for call encryption and streaming routing are not defined.
Call quality handling (adaptation for low bandwidth, network fallback) is missing.
Integration with patient scheduling and EHR virtual consult logs is not detailed.
In-call utilities (screen sharing, chat, file sharing of reports) are undefined.
clarification_questions: What streaming technology should be used (e.g., custom WebRTC media server, Twilio Video, or Agora)?
How do we ensure end-to-end call encryption and HIPAA compliance (e.g., no session recording, secure routing)?
What features should be available during the video call (e.g., text chat, PDF document viewing, screen sharing)?
What should the system do if a patient's internet connection is too slow for video?
How should the telemedicine session be initiated, and how are doctors and patients notified?
user_clarifications: Integrate Twilio Video API for WebRTC-based video sessions. No call recordings are allowed on servers.
Enforce end-to-end SRTP encryption. Media servers must comply with HIPAA BAA agreements.
In-call features must include peer-to-peer text chat, screen sharing (doctor only), and PDF review from the patient's EHR.
If bandwidth drops below 500kbps, automatically disable video stream and fallback to audio-only mode with user notification.
Sessions are triggered from the appointment schedule dashboard. Send email/SMS invite links 10 minutes prior.
refined_summary: Develop a HIPAA-compliant Telemedicine Video Call system integrating Twilio Video API with end-to-end SRTP encryption and no server recordings. The application will support screen sharing for doctors, text chat, EHR PDF sharing, bandwidth adaptation (auto-disabling video and falling back to audio-only under 500kbps), and automated invitation delivery 10 minutes before the scheduled time.
functional_requirements: The system shall create secure, temporary Twilio Video room tokens when a telehealth appointment is initiated.
The system shall display a secure overlay inside the video interface showing patient documents from the EHR.
The system shall allow the doctor to share their active screen window with the patient during the active WebRTC call.
The system shall monitor connection bitrates and toggle the client video camera off if bandwidth falls below 500kbps.
The system shall dispatch email and SMS notifications containing secure, single-use consultation links to both parties.
non_functional_requirements: Media connections must utilize Peer-to-Peer STUN/TURN servers to guarantee low latency (less than 200ms round-trip).
The chat channel messages must remain in memory and be permanently deleted immediately after the video room closes.
The system must comply with HIPAA Security Rules and SOC 2 guidelines, requiring a signed BAA from Twilio.
acceptance_criteria: Verify that clicking the invite link redirects both parties into a secure WebRTC video room without requiring app installation.
Verify that simulating network drop below 500kbps smoothly transitions the interface to audio-only mode and displays a warning toast.
Verify that no database records or server directories store text chat transcripts or raw video media files post-session.

raw_requirement: We need to support electronic prescribing so doctors can send prescriptions to pharmacies.
ambiguities: Integration with national e-prescribing networks (e.g., Surescripts) is not defined.
Drug-drug and drug-allergy interaction checking rules are unspecified.
Validation of doctor credentialing (NPI, DEA numbers) is missing.
The pharmacy directory look-up and selection workflow are not detailed.
Rules for controlled substances (EPCS requirements, two-factor authentication) are omitted.
clarification_questions: Which electronic prescribing network must we integrate with (e.g., Surescripts)?
Do we need an automated clinical decision support tool to check for drug-drug and drug-allergy interactions?
How should the system verify doctor eligibility and credentials (NPI, DEA numbers) before sending a prescription?
What parameters should be searchable in the pharmacy directory lookup (e.g., zip code, pharmacy chain, hours)?
Should the system support Electronic Prescribing of Controlled Substances (EPCS), and if so, what security is required?
user_clarifications: Integrate Surescripts API for prescription delivery. Pharmacy searches must filter by zip code, pharmacy name, and current open hours.
Yes, integrate the First Databank (FDB) API to perform real-time checks for drug-drug, drug-allergy, and drug-disease interactions.
Doctors must have verified NPI (National Provider Identifier) and DEA numbers. These must be checked against the NPPES registry.
Yes, Surescripts EPCS compliance is required. Controlled substances require dual-authorization (password plus a hardware token/biometric MFA).
Prescriptions must contain patient demographics, ICD-10 diagnosis code, drug name, strength, route, frequency, refills, and DAW (Dispense as Written) flags.
refined_summary: Design an e-prescribing system integrated with Surescripts and First Databank APIs. The system will validate doctor NPI and DEA numbers, support zipcode-based pharmacy lookups, perform automated drug-drug/allergy/disease interaction checks, and enforce Surescripts EPCS compliance using dual-factor authentication (biometrics/hardware token) for prescribing controlled substances.
functional_requirements: The system shall query Surescripts directory to locate pharmacies by location, chain name, and active status.
The system shall intercept prescription drafts and run them through the First Databank API to detect interactions with patient EHR allergies.
The system shall display a warning banner requiring doctor confirmation if a drug-allergy or drug-drug conflict is detected.
The system shall require dual-factor authentication (biometrics or physical key) prior to releasing EPCS schedules.
The system shall format and deliver Surescripts-compliant XML/JSON payloads to the target pharmacy system.
non_functional_requirements: Clinical decision checks (FDB API) must complete in under 500ms during the prescription authoring flow.
The system must comply with Surescripts certification standards and Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) rules.
All prescription records must retain audit histories for at least 10 years per federal guidelines.
acceptance_criteria: Verify that a physician attempting to prescribe penicillin to a patient with a documented penicillin allergy in the EHR is blocked by a critical warning modal.
Verify that submitting a controlled substance (e.g., Oxycodone) prompts for MFA and fails if the doctor's DEA number is invalid.
Verify that the selected pharmacy receives the prescription data and returns an receipt acknowledgement code via Surescripts within 3 seconds.

raw_requirement: We need to handle billing, verify patient insurance at checkout, and submit claims.
ambiguities: Supported clearinghouses (e.g., Change Healthcare, Waystar) for claims submission are not specified.
EDI transaction standards (e.g., HIPAA 270/271 for eligibility, 837P/837I for claims) are not defined.
Co-pay and deductible calculation rules are unspecified.
Handling of claim rejections and error-reporting workflows is missing.
Integration with patient payment processing for outstanding balances is omitted.
clarification_questions: Which insurance clearinghouse should we integrate with for claims processing?
Should the system handle electronic EDI transactions (e.g., 270/271 for eligibility checks, 837P/837I for submitting claims)?
How should co-pays, deductibles, and co-insurance be calculated and shown to the patient at checkout?
What is the workflow for billing coordinators when a claim is rejected or denied by a payer?
Should the portal allow patients to pay their co-pays online using credit cards or HSA/FSA cards?
user_clarifications: Integrate with Change Healthcare clearinghouse.
Yes, we must support ANSI ASC X12 EDI formats: 270/271 for real-time eligibility checks and 837P (Professional) for claims submission.
Calculate patient responsibility dynamically by querying the 271 response. Show co-pay, deductible remaining, and expected patient share.
Rejected claims must populate a workflow queue on the billing dashboard with the clearinghouse error codes highlighted for correction and resubmission.
Yes, integrate with Stripe to support online payments via Credit/Debit cards and HSA (Health Savings Account) / FSA (Flexible Spending Account) cards.
refined_summary: Develop a Billing & Insurance Claims system integrated with Change Healthcare clearinghouse. It must support EDI 270/271 transactions for real-time eligibility verification (showing copays and remaining deductibles) and EDI 837P for professional claims. Build a rejection correction queue for billing coordinators and integrate Stripe for credit/debit and HSA/FSA card payment processing.
functional_requirements: The system shall generate and transmit EDI 270 eligibility inquiries to Change Healthcare when a patient checks in.
The system shall parse EDI 271 responses and display copay, coinsurance, and deductible balances in the billing interface.
The system shall automatically generate EDI 837P claim files from completed clinical SOAP notes containing ICD-10 and CPT codes.
The system shall isolate rejected claims in a dedicated queue, parsing and mapping X12 error codes to human-readable issues.
The system shall process card payments via Stripe, validating card type eligibility for HSA/FSA classifications.
non_functional_requirements: Real-time EDI 270/271 eligibility inquiries must complete and display details in under 3 seconds.
Claims data batches must be securely packaged and transmitted using SFTP with SSH key authentication.
Payment interfaces must comply with PCI-DSS standards, utilizing tokenization for card data.
acceptance_criteria: Verify that clicking 'Verify Insurance' sends a 270 payload and successfully populates the copay and deductible fields from the 271 response.
Verify that submitting an incomplete claim missing a primary diagnosis code triggers validation block and pushes it to the billing correction queue.
Verify that attempting to pay with an invalid HSA card shows a payment decline message and logs the transaction error.

raw_requirement: Patients should be able to view their lab test results, and doctors need to review and sign off on them first.
ambiguities: Workflow for doctor sign-off (approval levels, clinical remarks) is not defined.
Handling of critical/abnormal results (delaying patient release, alert triggers) is unspecified.
Standard lab report format (PDF vs. structured tables vs. reference range graphs) is not chosen.
Notification mechanism for patients when lab results are ready is undefined.
Integration with external laboratory systems (e.g., Labcorp, Quest) is missing.
clarification_questions: How should the doctor review and sign off on lab results (e.g., e-signature, adding comments, flagging values)?
Should critical/abnormal lab results be released to patients immediately, or held for a buffer period (e.g., 48 hours) to allow doctor contact?
How should results be displayed to patients (e.g., PDF attachments or interactive charts comparing values against reference ranges)?
How should patients be notified when their results are ready (e.g., SMS, email)? Should notifications omit diagnostic details?
What laboratory system interfaces (e.g., HL7 ORU, LIONC coding) are required to ingest these results?
user_clarifications: Doctors must digitally sign off on all results, optionally adding patient-facing notes. Abnormal values must be highlighted in red.
Normal results are released immediately upon sign-off. Critical/abnormal results are held for 48 hours after doctor sign-off to allow direct phone outreach, unless released sooner by the physician.
Display results in structured tables with interactive line charts comparing patient data against normal reference ranges.
Notify patients via HIPAA-compliant emails and SMS alerts that say 'Your new lab results are ready to view. Please log in to your secure portal.' (Do not include actual test names or results).
Ingest results using HL7 ORU messages containing LOINC (Logical Observation Identifiers Names and Codes) identifiers.
refined_summary: Implement a Lab Results Portal structured with LOINC coding and HL7 ORU ingestion. Doctors must sign off and add comments before results release, highlighting abnormal values in red. Normal results release immediately; critical results have a 48-hour hold for patient outreach unless overridden. Display interactive charts comparing results to reference ranges, sending notifications containing no clinical details.
functional_requirements: The system shall display incoming HL7 ORU lab results in the physician's review dashboard.
The system shall require the doctor's electronic signature and lock the record before releasing results to the patient portal.
The system shall implement a 48-hour release delay countdown timer for results flagged as 'Critical' or 'Abnormal'.
The system shall render comparison graphs plotting LOINC test values against standard high/low reference ranges.
The system shall send email and SMS alerts via SendGrid/Twilio notifying the patient of results availability without displaying PHI.
non_functional_requirements: Patient lab pages must load and display interactive results charts in less than 1.5 seconds.
The digital signature module must use cryptographically validated signing keys to ensure non-repudiation.
All lab data transmissions from external labs must be verified using HMAC signature validation headers.
acceptance_criteria: Verify that a patient cannot see their lab results in the portal until the doctor clicks 'Sign and Release' on the dashboard.
Verify that an abnormal blood panel result remains hidden from the patient portal for 48 hours after sign-off, unless the doctor selects 'Release Immediately'.
Verify that the SMS notification received by the patient contains only a login link and no mention of the specific lab tests (e.g., 'Cholesterol Panel').

raw_requirement: We want to sync data from patient wearables like heart monitors and alert doctors if something is wrong.
ambiguities: Supported wearable brands and device APIs (Apple HealthKit, Fitbit, Dexcom) are not specified.
Definition of 'something is wrong' (vital threshold limits, duration of abnormal readings) is undefined.
The frequency of data sync (real-time stream vs. hourly/daily batch sync) is unclear.
The alert routing escalation path (alerting the on-call nurse, doctor, or emergency services) is missing.
Handling of noisy data or connection drops (preventing alert fatigue) is omitted.
clarification_questions: Which wearable platforms must we integrate with (e.g., Apple HealthKit, Google Fit, Dexcom CGMs)?
How are the vital threshold alerts configured (e.g., heart rate > 120 bpm for 5 minutes, or individual patient customized limits)?
What is the required data synchronization frequency (e.g., real-time WebSockets vs. batch uploads every 15 minutes)?
If an alert is triggered, who gets notified first, and what is the escalation workflow if they do not respond?
How do we filter out noise (e.g., a loose sensor causing a zero heart rate reading) to prevent false alerts?
user_clarifications: Integrate with Apple HealthKit (via iOS App) and Dexcom CGM API for glucose levels.
Alert thresholds must be customizable per patient in their EHR profile, with default safe ranges (e.g., Heart Rate: 50-100 bpm, Glucose: 70-180 mg/dL).
Sync heart rate data every 5 minutes from Apple HealthKit, and glucose data every 5 minutes from Dexcom.

If vitals cross thresholds for 3 consecutive readings (to filter out noise), trigger a push notification to the on-call nurse. If unacknowledged within 10 minutes, escalate to the primary care physician.
Filter out extreme, physically impossible spikes (e.g., HR = 0 or > 250) as sensor errors; log them but do not trigger notifications.
refined_summary: Develop a Patient Monitoring system integrating Apple HealthKit and Dexcom CGM APIs. Sync data every 5 minutes, checking values against customizable patient EHR thresholds. If readings cross thresholds for 3 consecutive cycles (excluding physical anomalies), alert the on-call nurse via push notifications, escalating to the primary physician after 10 minutes if unacknowledged.
functional_requirements: The system shall ingest heart rate data from HealthKit and glucose readings from Dexcom every 5 minutes.
The system shall validate incoming vital readings against the patient's specific EHR threshold configurations.
The system shall implement a sliding window filter that counts consecutive out-of-bounds readings and ignores outliers.
The system shall send push notifications using APNS/FCM to on-call nursing staff when thresholds are breached.
The system shall escalate notifications to the patient's primary care physician if the nurse does not click 'Acknowledge' within 10 minutes.
non_functional_requirements: The vital event processing pipeline must evaluate incoming streams and trigger alerts within 3 seconds of data ingestion.
The IoT ingestion gateway must support horizontal scaling to handle up to 50,000 active telemetry streams concurrently.
Alert notification logs must be stored in a high-availability database with audit trails showing the response times of clinical staff.
acceptance_criteria: Verify that if a patient's heart rate is reported as 110, 115, and 120 bpm (threshold is 100) over three consecutive readings, an alert is sent to the nurse.
Verify that a single heart rate reading of 0 followed by normal readings does not trigger an alert.
Verify that if the nurse fails to acknowledge a critical alert within 10 minutes, the primary care physician receives a priority email/SMS notification.

raw_requirement: We need a scheduler for hospital shifts, doctor rotations, and handling swap requests.
ambiguities: Labor compliance rules (e.g., maximum consecutive hours, mandatory rest periods) are not defined.
The workflow for approving shift swaps (automatic approval vs. supervisor sign-off) is unspecified.
Support for varying shift roles (on-call, resident, attending, surgeon) is missing.
Handling of emergency call-outs and backup rotation rules is unclear.
Calendar viewing permissions (department-specific views vs. hospital-wide) are omitted.
clarification_questions: What labor laws and hospital safety guidelines must be enforced (e.g., max 12-hour shifts, 11 hours rest between shifts)?
What is the workflow for shift swap requests? Can colleagues swap directly if they have the same role, or is admin approval mandatory?
What shift roles and department groupings need to be supported?
How should the system handle emergency sick-leave call-outs? Does it recommend qualified on-call backups?
Who is allowed to edit the master schedule vs. viewing the schedule?
user_clarifications: Enforce a maximum of 16 consecutive work hours and a mandatory minimum rest period of 12 hours between shifts. Maximum weekly hours cannot exceed 80.

If an employee calls out sick, the system must query the active on-call list for that department/role and present a list of eligible replacements sorted by current weekly hours (lowest first).
Department Chiefs and Schedulers have write access. Staff have read-only access to their department and personal schedules.
refined_summary: Implement a Doctor/Staff Scheduling system with strict labor rule enforcement (max 16 consecutive hours, min 12 hours rest, max 80 weekly hours). The system must support role-based shift assignments across departments, validate shift swap requests (requiring Department Chief approval), and manage an emergency backup list sorted by lowest weekly hours for sick call-outs.
functional_requirements: The system shall block schedulers from assigning shifts that violate configured labor rest buffers or hour limits.
The system shall provide a shift swap portal where staff can search for eligible swap partners and submit requests.
The system shall route validated shift-swap requests to the Department Chief dashboard for approval.
The system shall generate a prioritized list of on-call staff to cover sick calls based on qualification and weekly hours.
The system shall display a read-only calendar for staff, customizable with department and role filters.
non_functional_requirements: Shift validation logic checks must complete in under 300ms during manual schedule editing.
The calendar interface must update and sync schedule changes in real-time using server-sent events (SSE).
Schedule revision histories must be logged, showing who changed which shift and when.
acceptance_criteria: Verify that attempting to assign a doctor to a shift that starts 10 hours after their last shift ends displays a rule violation warning and blocks the save.
Verify that a shift swap between a Pediatric Resident and a Cardiology Resident is blocked because the departments and specialties do not match.
Verify that when a nurse logs a sick call, the system displays the correct on-call nurse list sorted by lowest weekly hours.

raw_requirement: Design a system to refer patients to specialists, send their medical files securely, and track appointment completion.
ambiguities: Supported communication channels/standards (Direct Messaging, HL7 CCDA, secure email) are not defined.
Data filtering rules (how to redact irrelevant or sensitive patient history from the referral file) are unspecified.
The verification loop (how we track if the patient actually booked and completed the specialist visit) is unclear.
Insurance pre-authorization rules for referrals are omitted.
Security compliance for file transit (HIPAA requirements, encryption levels) is not specified.
clarification_questions: What security standard should be used to transmit referral files (e.g., Direct Secure Messaging protocol, HL7 CCDA attachments, or secure portal-to-portal)?
How should the referring physician select what parts of the patient's medical record are sent to the specialist?
How is the completion of the referral tracked? Does the specialist system send a status update?
Do referrals require insurance pre-authorization validation before they are released?
What notifications are sent to patients to guide them in booking the specialist appointment?
user_clarifications: Transmit records as HL7 CCDA (Continuity of Care Document) files over the Direct Secure Messaging protocol (Direct Project standards).
The system must present a checkbox interface allowing the referring doctor to select/deselect clinical notes, lab results, and medications.
Referrals must track four statuses: Draft, Submitted, Appointment Booked, Consultation Completed. The specialist portal must send a CCDA consultation note back to update status to Completed.
Yes, referrals must include a field for prior authorization codes, showing status as 'Pending Authorization' until updated by billing.
Send secure portal messages and automated emails containing specialist contact info, the referral letter, and instructions.
refined_summary: Design a Referral Management system transmitting HL7 CCDA documents over the Direct Secure Messaging protocol. The system will feature an EHR section checklist for selective data attachment, track four referral statuses (Draft, Submitted, Booked, Completed via specialist consultation note feedback), manage insurance prior authorization fields, and deliver booking instructions to patients.
functional_requirements: The system shall compile EHR data into standardized XML-based HL7 CCDA documents based on physician selections.
The system shall send CCDA packets securely via Direct Secure Messaging (SMIME/SMTP integration).
The system shall update referral status to 'Appointment Booked' upon receiving an scheduling message from the specialist.
The system shall parse incoming consultation reports from specialists and link them to the original referral record to change status to 'Completed'.
The system shall flag referrals requiring prior authorization, routing them to the insurance coordinator's checklist.
non_functional_requirements: CCDA generation and validation must execute in less than 2.0 seconds.
All outbound emails to patients must encrypt PHI links, using AES-256 with URL tokens that expire in 7 days.
The Direct Messaging mail client must hold certified credentials complying with ONC Health IT requirements.
acceptance_criteria: Verify that deselecting 'Lab Results' in the referral form excludes the lab result section from the generated HL7 CCDA XML payload.
Verify that receiving a consultation note back from the specialist updates the patient's referral status to 'Consultation Completed' and adds the note to the EHR.
Verify that a referral flagged as 'Requires Auth' remains in 'Pending Authorization' status and blocks transmission until the auth code is entered.

raw_requirement: We need to send text messages and emails to patients about their clinical updates without leaking private info.
ambiguities: The boundaries of what constitutes Protected Health Information (PHI) in notifications are undefined.
The opt-out and consent mechanisms for receiving text alerts are unspecified.
The integration with communication gateways (e.g., Twilio, SendGrid) and security configurations are unclear.
The authentication mechanism for reading detailed notifications (secure login vs. tokenized links) is not defined.
Handling of message delivery failures or expired links is omitted.
clarification_questions: What specific types of clinical updates will trigger notifications (e.g., prescription ready, new message, lab results)?
What exact details can be included in the SMS and email text without violating HIPAA?
How do patients consent to or opt-out of SMS and email communications?
Should the notification link direct the patient to log in, or can it use a secure, temporary landing page?
What security measures must be in place for our Twilio and SendGrid integrations (e.g., TLS encryption, signed BAAs)?
user_clarifications: Triggers: appointment reminders, new portal messages, prescription ready, and lab results signed off.
SMS and emails must not contain any PHI, diagnosis names, medication names, or doctor specialties. Use generic text (e.g., 'Your prescription is ready' instead of 'Your Lipitor is ready').
Patients must opt-in to SMS alerts during portal registration, and can opt-out by texting 'STOP' or updating portal preferences.
Links in notifications must redirect patients to a secure portal login page. Do not display any health details on unauthenticated pages.

refined_summary: Implement a HIPAA-Compliant Notification system using Twilio and SendGrid. functional_requirements: The system shall trigger SMS and email events using standardized templates devoid of PHI data.
The system shall check patient consent preferences in the database before dispatching any SMS alerts.
The system shall process 'STOP' replies from Twilio SMS webhooks, immediately updating the user's opt-out settings.
The system shall direct all notification action links to the authenticated portal login screen.
The system shall log delivery events, timestamps, and message IDs without logging the message text bodies.
non_functional_requirements: All outbound API calls to Twilio and SendGrid must enforce TLS 1.3.
The system must process opt-out updates in under 2 seconds to ensure compliance with TCPA guidelines.
No message bodies or text history containing PHI may be stored on the notification server logs.
acceptance_criteria: Verify that a prescription ready SMS states 'Your prescription is ready for pickup at Clinic Pharmacy' and does not mention the drug name.

functional_requirements: The system shall record physician voice dictation via the browser microphone and upload audio segments to a secure transit folder.
The system shall call Amazon Transcribe Medical API to generate structured transcriptions of the audio dictations.
The system shall process raw transcription texts with a LLM mapping prompt to distribute content into SOAP fields.

refined_summary: Implement a Medical Inventory Management system utilizing GS1 and NDC barcodes to track lot numbers and expiration dates. functional_requirements: The system shall parse GS1 and NDC barcode scans to identify items, lot numbers, and expiration dates.
The system shall decrement item inventory when a matching administration event is confirmed in the patient EHR chart.
The system shall require biometric or secondary credentials from two separate nurses before marking controlled substances as 'Dispensed'.
The system shall generate purchase requisitions for items falling below safety stock limits, queuing them for manager approval.
The system shall record temperature logs from connected pharmacy fridges and alert staff if readings fall outside 2-8°C.
non_functional_requirements: The dispensing database must use strict transaction locks to prevent concurrent stock adjustments of the same lot.
The narcotics digital ledger must be read-only for standard users and compile audited transaction chains.
The refrigeration alert notification must dispatch to maintenance staff via SMS within 30 seconds of an out-of-range temperature log.
acceptance_criteria: Verify that scanning an expired medication barcode triggers a critical warning modal and blocks the dispensing action.
Verify that dispensing a narcotic (e.g., Fentanyl) blocks progress until both the administering nurse and witness nurse authenticate their logins.
Verify that when inventory of surgical gloves falls below 10 boxes, a purchase requisition is automatically generated in the manager's inbox.

functional_requirements: The system shall compile CMS-compliant MIPS quality metrics payloads in structured XML formats.
The system shall strip all HIPAA Safe Harbor identifiers from export files generated by standard administrative staff.
The system shall calculate and display Hospital Operational KPIs (wait times, bed occupancy, ALOS) with daily trends.

refined_summary: Design a Pharmacy Order Fulfillment system supporting NCPDP D.0 insurance adjudication. Implement a mandatory three-step NDC scan verification workflow. functional_requirements: The system shall transmit insurance claims payloads in NCPDP D.0 formats and return copay requirements.

non_functional_requirements: NCPDP insurance adjudication transactions must resolve and return values in under 4 seconds.
The pharmacy scanner integration must recognize barcode inputs and update UI states within 150ms.
Signature storage must utilize cryptographically secure PDF formats with audit records.
acceptance_criteria: Verify that a pharmacist scanning a stock bottle NDC code that does not match the prescribed drug NDC receives a block alert.
Verify that completing checkout at the counter uploads a signature PDF to the patient file showing the HIPAA notice text.
Verify that changing order status to 'Ready for Pickup' sends a localized SMS to the patient's verified mobile number.

Verify that changing research consent to 'No' instantly drops that patient's records from all active research search exports.

Implement mandatory MFA for domestic transfers over $1,000 and all SWIFT wires.
functional_requirements: The system shall display transaction inputs for recipient routing number, bank name, account number, Swift BIC, and country.

non_functional_requirements: FedNow transaction confirmations must complete within 3 seconds of user approval.

acceptance_criteria: Verify that a customer attempting a $2,000 domestic transfer is prompted for MFA and the transfer is blocked if MFA fails.

refined_summary: Implement a Bill Pay and Scheduled Payments module integrated with Mastercard Bill Pay for national billers and supporting custom payee check printing. functional_requirements: The system shall query the Mastercard Bill Pay directory to match national billers.

The system shall calculate upcoming payment dates based on selected recurrence frequencies (weekly, monthly, etc.).

Integrate with Sift Science for fraud scoring and analysis.

Apply a tiered markup spread (1.0% under $10,000; 0.5% for $10,000+), block all negative balances or overdrafts in secondary currencies, and flag transactions exceeding $10,000 USD equivalent for AML compliance review.

Yes, native FaceID/TouchID must be supported for biometric quick login on iOS and Android after initial device registration.
refined_summary: Implement a secure Access Control and MFA module. It will support SMS/Email OTP and TOTP, alongside mobile biometrics (FaceID/TouchID). MFA is triggered on new device logins and as a step-up validation for high-value actions or profile updates. Enforce a 12-character complex password policy and lock accounts for 30 minutes after 5 failed attempts, with secure recovery flows.
functional_requirements: The system shall authenticate users using credentials checked against hashed values (bcrypt/argon2).
The system shall enforce MFA verification if the user logs in from an IP or device not registered in their trusted device list.
The system shall prompt for step-up verification (e.g., TOTP or SMS code) before executing transfers exceeding $1,000.

Refund transactions will deduct points, with support for negative reward balances.
functional_requirements: The system shall calculate points earned for each posted credit card transaction, applying category multipliers.
